report:
Based on my research, the current evidence does **not** support that ivermectin lowers the risk of death in COVID-19.

**Large randomized controlled trials (RCTs)** — the gold standard for medical evidence — have repeatedly failed to show benefit. A high-dose ivermectin trial published in *JAMA* (March 2023) found no improvement in time to sustained recovery among outpatients with mild-to-moderate COVID-19 compared to placebo, and concluded that the findings "do not support the use of ivermectin" in such patients ([JAMA, 2023](https://jamanetwork.com/journals/jama/fullarticle/2801827)). The UK's PRINCIPLE trial similarly met futility thresholds for ivermectin ([factually.co summary](https://factually.co/fact-checks/health/ivermectin-covid19-randomized-trials-2023-2025-results-b3742b)). A 2024 systematic review of RCTs found no significant reduction in hospitalization or all-cause mortality ([ScienceDirect, 2024](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0924857924001663)).

**Major health authorities** concur. The FDA has not approved ivermectin for COVID-19 and states that available clinical trial data "do not demonstrate that ivermectin is effective against COVID-19 in humans" ([Drugs.com/FDA](https://www.drugs.com/ivermectin.html)). The Infectious Diseases Society of America recommends against its use outside clinical trials ([Healio](https://www.healio.com/news/primary-care/20201208/this-was-a-gift-to-us-ivermectin-effective-for-covid19-prophylaxis-treatment)).

Some early meta-analyses and advocacy sites (e.g., c19early.org) claimed mortality reductions, but these have been criticized for relying heavily on small, low-quality, or retracted studies. When large, well-designed RCTs were completed, the apparent benefit disappeared — a pattern explained in detail by *The Atlantic* ([2021](https://www.theatlantic.com/science/archive/2021/10/ivermectin-research-problems/620473/)).

**Conclusion:** The best available evidence from large RCTs and major health authorities indicates ivermectin does **not** reduce the risk of death from COVID-19.
